Water is being poured into a rectangular prism shaped tank. The length and width of this tank are $8\text{ m}$ and $4\text{ m},$ respectively. If the height of the water increases at a rate of $0.25\text{ m/hour}$, determine the rate at which the volume of stored water increases.

A sugar cube is dissolving uniformly in water. If each edge of the cube decreases at a rate of $4\,\text{cm}/\text{s},$ determine the rate at which its volume is decreasing when the length of each edge is $2\,\text{cm}.$ Assume that the rate of decrease of the volume is positive.

The volume of the cube is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
${\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the side length of the cube and let $V$ be its volume. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-4\text{ cm/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}$ when $x=2\text{ cm}.$

We start with the formula for the volume of the cube:

$$
V={x}^{3}
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug $x=2$ and $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-4\text{ cm/s}$ into the expression for $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3(2)^{2}\cdot (-4) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =-48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the cube is decreasing at a rate of $48\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s}$ at the moment when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$
